cards.text: Jesus is sending out His twelve disciples, and He's been honest with them: if people called the head of the house Beelzebul, they'll call His household worse. Then He says, "So do not be afraid of them." Friend, I spent YEARS flinching every time that junk drawer rattled open, so I am LEANING in for this one.

cards.question: Jesus gives His disciples a reason not to fear the people against them. What does He say about everything concealed and hidden?

answers.text: It will all be made known
It will stay hidden for good

cards.text: Then Jesus talks about what He tells His disciples in the dark. The quiet stuff. The lean-in-close, whispered-in-your-ear stuff.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus tells His disciples to keep what He whispers to them a secret.

cards.text: NOPE. What's whispered in their ear, they speak in the daylight and proclaim from the housetops, which is the exact OPPOSITE of my volume when I admit I ate the cookie dough.
Then Jesus names the worst the people against them can do: kill the body. But He says there's something they can't reach.

cards.question: They can kill the body, but Jesus says they cannot kill the ___.
So instead of fearing those who kill the body, who does Jesus tell His disciples to fear?

answers.text: The One who can destroy soul and body
The governors who judge them in court
The councils that hand them over

cards.text: Then Jesus asks, "Are not two sparrows sold for a penny?" Friend, I went for 25 cents out of a bakery bin, and even I hear that and go, that's a BARGAIN.

cards.question: Two sparrows, one penny. True or false: Jesus says not one of them falls to the ground apart from the will of the Father.

cards.text: Then Jesus says even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. Friend, I walk around with a mustache I use as HANDS, and every single hair is counted. EVERY one.

cards.question: Sparrows cared for and hairs all numbered. What does Jesus tell His disciples they're worth?

answers.text: About the same as two sparrows

cards.text: Then Jesus says everyone who confesses Him before men, He will also confess before His Father in heaven.

cards.question: And the other side: whoever ___ Jesus before men, Jesus will also deny before His Father in heaven.

cards.text: Then Jesus says something that'll make you set the rolling pin down: don't assume He came to bring peace to the earth.

cards.question: Jesus says He has not come to bring peace. What does He say He has come to bring?

cards.text: Jesus says He has come to turn a man against his father, a daughter against her mother, a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says a man's enemies will be the members of his own household.

cards.text: Then Jesus sets the order. Anyone who loves father or mother, or son or daughter, more than Him is not worthy of Him.

cards.question: Jesus says anyone who doesn't take up something and follow Him isn't worthy of Him. What does a follower take up?

cards.text: Then Jesus says, "Whoever finds his life will lose it," and just lets that sit there. Like a cookie you can't tell is done yet.

cards.question: And whoever loses his life for Jesus' sake will ___ it.

cards.text: Now Jesus talks about the people the disciples will meet out there, the ones who receive them and welcome them in. Friend, I spent years waiting on a drawer to open, so I've got FEELINGS about this one.

cards.question: When someone receives the disciples, who else does Jesus say they receive?

answers.text: Jesus and the One who sent Him

cards.text: Then Jesus talks rewards, starting with someone who receives a prophet because he is a prophet.

cards.question: Someone receives a prophet because he is a prophet. True or false: Jesus says that person will receive a prophet's reward.

cards.text: Same goes for receiving a righteous man because he is a righteous man. Then Jesus goes small, I mean SMALL: even a cup of cold water, given to one of these little ones because he's His disciple.

cards.question: Even for one cup of cold water, Jesus says that giver will never lose his ___.
After Jesus finishes instructing His twelve disciples, what does He do next?

answers.text: Teaches and preaches in their cities
Rests for a while in Capernaum
Goes up a mountain alone to pray

findings.problem: In Matthew 10:27, Jesus gives the disciples a command: 'speak in the daylight... proclaim from the housetops.' The card says 'they speak in the daylight and proclaim from the housetops,' which reads as a report of what they do, not a command. It also merges the text's two pairings (dark to daylight, whispered to housetops) into one.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Calling killing the body 'the worst the people against them can do' is an interpretation. Matthew 10:28 only says they can kill the body but cannot kill the soul.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The question opens with 'And the other side:', which points back to the confess line on card 13. That card is no longer on screen.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The question already says 'Jesus will also deny,' so the blank can only be 'denies.' That wording rules out 'follows' and 'welcomes,' and the right answer echoes a word printed in the question.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'And just lets that sit there' says Jesus paused. In Matthew 10:39, the next clause ('and whoever loses his life for My sake will find it') follows in the same sentence, so the line adds a fact the text doesn't support.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can add a storyteller's line to carry the moment, like "But the Lord isn't finished with him," as long as it adds no facts.

findings.problem: The comparison doesn't match the action. A saying that sounds backwards (finding your life means losing it) is not the same as being unsure whether a cookie is done, so the image doesn't click right away.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The core action of the verse is receiving and welcoming someone. The joke is about waiting for a drawer to open, which is waiting to be found, not welcoming. Papa Dorin welcoming newcomers to the drawer would match the action. As written, the link is unclear.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: Almost every joke uses the same template, 'Friend, I [backstory fact]...' (stop 1 cards 1, 9 and 11; stop 2 card 9), and two of them are 'I spent years' drawer lines. The humor follows a formula instead of fitting each moment.

rule.text: No formula. His personality fits whatever moment he's in, whether it's a tense moment in a story, a hard teaching or a quick question. There are no joke quotas and no required kinds of jokes.

findings.problem: Many story cards are plain retelling with no voice: stop 1 cards 3, 6 and 13, and stop 2 cards 3, 5 and 11. Several of the jokes are only mildly pleasant: the rolling pin line (stop 2 card 1) and 'I mean SMALL' (stop 2 card 13). The walkthrough rarely reaches a laugh-out-loud moment.

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
